author: pallas, 1776
summary: 전국에서 흔히 겨울을 나는 겨울새로, 산지의 숲이나 농경지에서 지낸다. 보통 홀로 또는 암수가 함께 지내며, 벼과 식물의 씨를 즐겨 먹고 여름철에는 곤충도 즐겨 먹는다. 시베리아 툰드라 일대에서 번식하는데, 나무 밑이나 풀숲에 잔가지와 풀줄기로 밥그릇 모양 둥지를 짓고 한배에 알 4~6개를 낳는다. 중국 동북 지방과 한국에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: broad deep buff supercilium from bill base to nape

art.subject: Siberian Accentor (Prunella montanella), adult in winter, as seen in Korea from November to March: crown blackish-brown; a very broad deep ochre-buff supercilium running from the bill base over the eye to the nape; black ear-coverts forming a dark mask below the supercilium; grey patch on the side of the neck; back and scapulars warm brown boldly streaked blackish-brown; wings brown with rufous fringes and a thin pale wing-bar; throat and breast deep ochre-buff, belly paler buff; flanks streaked chestnut. Thin, sharply pointed dark bill; dark eye; orange-pink legs.
art.pose: foraging on the ground for grass seeds, side view
art.scene: Korean winter farmland edge beside a mountain woodland; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in winter, side view on the ground: blackish crown and ear-coverts, broad deep buff supercilium from bill base to nape, grey neck sides, brown back streaked blackish-brown, ochre-buff underparts, chestnut-streaked flanks, thin pointed bill
adult, head detail in side view: broad ochre-buff supercilium running unbroken from the bill base past the crown to the nape, black ear-covert mask, ochre-buff throat, fine pointed dark bill
art.build: Small, plump, sparrow-sized accentor, 15cm, with a rounded head with no crest and a short neck; creeps low on the ground and in low bushes with a rather horizontal stance, picking up small seeds. Bill short, thin and finely pointed like a warbler's, clearly shorter than the head, not a seed-cracking cone. Legs medium length, orange-pink. Tail medium length, square-ended, plain brown without white.
avoid: Do not paint a thick conical bunting bill; accentors have a thin, pointed bill.
Do not add a crest, a black breast patch or white outer tail feathers; those belong to Yellow-throated Bunting (Emberiza elegans), which has a similar black-and-yellow head.
Do not make the supercilium white or lemon-yellow; it is deep ochre-buff.
Do not streak the throat or breast heavily; the streaks are mainly on the back and flanks.
